briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 16, 2026. Today has been a day marked by a convergence of international policy setbacks surrounding climate change and proactive response efforts both domestically and internationally.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Policy Reversals and Intensifying Crisis
sections.content: According to news released today, there have been domestic and international reports indicating that the Trump administration plans to abolish key power plant carbon regulations and eliminate greenhouse gas regulations through the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) [1, 73]. Such policy reversals pose significant challenges to climate change response efforts. Meanwhile, major floods in Nepal and Tibet have been declared climate disasters, prompting requests for emergency international funding [6, 76, 93]. Research findings also indicate worsening snow droughts in Nevada [74], further clarifying the reality of the global climate crisis. Wisconsin doctors are warning that climate change is making people sick [80], and analyses suggest it could even incite impulsive behavior [81], raising growing concerns about climate change's impact extending beyond a mere environmental issue to affect society as a whole.

sections.title: 🌱 Diverse Efforts for Achieving Domestic Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Amidst these crises, proactive movements towards a carbon-neutral society continue domestically. The Climate Change Foundation hosted a forum on utilizing regional carbon neutrality data [2], and the National Climate Crisis Response Committee held a forum commemorating the approval of the IPCC Synthesis Report [3], strengthening knowledge sharing and cooperation for climate change response. Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance is accelerating its climate response despite achieving record performance [4], and Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) is leading carbon neutrality with nuclear power and hydrogen, winning the ESG Grand Prize for three consecutive years [21]. Furthermore, various local governments, including Gunpo City, Naju City, and Buk-gu of Jeonnam Gwangju Integrated Special City, have been recognized as excellent cases in carbon neutrality and awarded ministerial prizes [16, 20, 23, 29, 31], demonstrating the fruition of regional-level efforts. Activities encouraging citizen participation are also vibrant, such as Cheonan City and Hoseo University jointly conducting a carbon neutrality practice campaign [14, 25], and Gangnam-gu hosting a carbon neutrality experience festival [33].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Technological Innovation
sections.content: Significant progress has also been made in the renewable energy sector. Naver has partnered with Geurin Energy to secure renewable energy for its data centers, investing in a 216MW solar project and agreeing to long-term power purchase [37, 38, 40, 45, 46, 48, 49, 50, 51, 53, 55, 59, 65, 66]. This is a crucial example of accelerating the renewable energy transition while addressing the increasing power demand of AI data centers. Jeju Development Corporation has installed 204.8kW of solar power at its Samdasoo second water intake facility [54], and the Seoul Metropolitan Area's largest industrial complex rooftop solar power system, 12.6MW, has been completed at Siheung Oido Steel Land [56]. The Korea Power Exchange is inspecting the Anjwa BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) construction site, laying the groundwork for stable integration of renewable energy [52], and efforts for innovative technological development, such as renewable energy storage solutions utilizing underground rocks [58], are also continuing. These investments and technological innovations are expected to contribute to domestic energy security and the achievement of carbon neutrality goals, along with an analysis that renewable energy acts as an 'economic breakwater' against geopolitical energy shocks, resulting in savings of 4.4 trillion won in fossil fuel electricity purchase costs [39].

sections.title: ⚠️ Climate Change Response: Complex Challenges and International Implications
sections.content: However, addressing climate change still presents a multitude of complex challenges. At a seminar by the National Assembly Climate Change Forum, an analysis indicated that Korea's bilateral cooperation has lower flexibility compared to major countries [7]. Furthermore, it was pointed out that for carbon neutrality in the construction sector, carbon emissions must first be clearly identified [10]. Issues such as the inefficient use of surplus electricity [64] and the mixed performance of the renewable energy stock market [60] underscore the importance of stable operation of renewable energy systems and fostering an attractive investment environment. Internationally, setbacks in policy and education have also been observed, with the Texas A&M System removing climate change courses from its core curriculum [72] and a federal court invalidating New York's climate change Superfund law [78]. Meanwhile, reports that Mark Cuban asked what would destroy humanity between AI and climate change, and Grok did not hesitate [92], illustrate the fundamental questions the climate crisis poses to humanity and its complex relationship with other technological threats. Amidst these challenges, the move by Bristol City in the UK to ban advertisements for fast fashion, SUVs, and airlines, aiming for a complete ban on advertising from polluting industries [96], offers new implications for strengthening social regulations in response to climate change.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has clearly illustrated the reality where hope and concern coexist regarding climate change. Amidst international policy setbacks and intensifying climate disasters, we have seen continuous efforts from various stakeholders, both domestically and internationally, striving for carbon neutrality and the transition to renewable energy. Our journey to overcome the climate crisis will continue to face complex challenges, but consistent action based on scientific facts and international cooperation are more crucial than ever. This concludes today's climate briefing.
